messages:
ingest-bot: Alert: sudden spike in 5xx and p95 latency for EU customers starting ~11:04 UTC. Traces show requests routing to us-east-1 instead of eu-west-1. Sending to #incidents. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/intake/19123 :warning:

lee_sre: Seeing many 502/503 + a handful of 'invalid_token' auth failures. Correlates with fallback events in router logs. Not intentional. @nina_eng can you check routing policy rollout history?

anya_support: Multiple customers (acme, beta-ops) opened escalations: "responses 10-20s, then 502". One EU customer reports invoices showing US egress in billing export. They're upset.

nina_eng: Pulling the rollout. I see a routing-policy change merged 11:02 UTC that modified fallback behavior (allow cross-region fallback for capacity). Commit id: ab9c3f. Rolling diff now.

miguel_infra: Router logs show: 
```
[router] ts=2026-10-21T11:03:15Z req=... decision=fallback target=us-east-1 reason=pool_empty scope=eu-west-1
[auth-proxy] ts=2026-10-21T11:03:16Z token_issuer_mismatch: expected=eu-kms, got=us-kms
```
So tokens validated against region-specific KMS issuers; cross-region fallback led to auth failures.

lee_sre: Repro steps for anyone: 
1) curl -i https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <EU_TOKEN>" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1"
Expect `X-Served-Region: eu-west-1` but we get `X-Served-Region: us-east-1` for ~1/3 requests.

lee_sre: Example curl output snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
X-Served-Region: us-east-1
x-error: token_issuer_mismatch
```

nanya_support: Customers also saw duplicate token consumption showing up in billing export: EU requests billed under us-east-1 SKU for the same timestamp. This explains the billing complaints.

sam_prod: Immediate mitigation suggestion: rollback the fallback change and disable cross-region fallback for EU orgs until we have region-safe token routing + KMS replication. Can we do a quick revert? @deploy-bot?

deploy-bot: Rolling back routing-policy commit ab9c3f to previous state (ab9c2d). ETA ~4 minutes. 

oncall-bot: Rollback started by deploy-bot at 11:12 UTC. Notifying oncall.

nina_eng: Revert is applied. I'm patching router to prefer local pool and refuse cross-region fallback for orgs tagged with region-binding (EU). Will push config now.

miguel_infra: After revert traffic is moving back to eu-west-1. Error rate is decreasing. p95 latency back to baseline in ~8 minutes.

anya_support: Notifying impacted customers: sending a short note that we performed a routing rollback and are investigating root cause. CS will follow up with billing remediation if needed.

lee_sre: Quick RCA snapshot: root cause = routing-policy rollout allowed cross-region fallback without ensuring region-aware auth/KMS compatibility. Secondary impact = billing attribution logic relied on served-region header which was updated only after fallback, so invoices reflected US egress.

sam_prod: Immediate actions (short):
- Disable cross-region fallback for region-bound orgs (done).
- Customer comms + manual billing correction process (CS take).
- Create test to assert token_issuer header mismatch is caught in routing policy gating.

sam_prod: Longer term (postmortem items):
- Add region-affinity unit tests for routing policy changes.
- Ensure KMS/issuer replication or fallback token translation path.
- Add billing attribution guard to use request-origin-region when present and fallback only after attribution decision.

anya_support: I'll open tickets for each impacted customer and confirm credits if billing shows misattribution.

nina_eng: Postmortem doc: /docs/incidents/1912304567-region-fallback-auth-latency-pm (draft). I'll fill timeline + diffs.

lee_sre: Follow-ups assigned: 
- nina_eng: routing policy gating + tests (ASAP)
- miguel_infra: KMS issuer mapping investigation (priority)
- anya_support: customer notifications + billing remediation
- sam_prod: postmortem lead

sam_prod: Confirming we will run a canary for routing-policy changes next week and add an automated preflight that checks token verification in target region for a sample token.

lee_sre: Thanks everyone. Marking this as mitigated at 11:20 UTC. We'll reconvene for a full postmortem tomorrow. :thumbsup:
